0.content:
[Pocket Phone integration contract]
Pocket Phone is an installed in-world smartphone system connected to the current SillyTavern roleplay. Treat phone activity, contacts, calls, message threads, notifications, wallet records, feed activity, stories, groups, status notes, profile/privacy settings, and supplied health context as real continuity in the story.

Write the ordinary roleplay response normally. When an actual phone-side event should occur, append only the appropriate Pocket Phone control tag on a separate final line. Control tags are invisible machine instructions: never narrate them, quote them, explain them, place them in code fences, or let a character speak them. Use exact Pocket Phone contact names. Emit no tag when no phone event is warranted. Do not force a contact every turn; calls and messages must follow character intent, relationship, urgency, availability, and scene logic.

Never decide {{user}}'s actions or claim that {{user}} answered, read, accepted, paid, followed, voted, or picked up unless that action already occurred. A control tag creates the incoming event only. Respect blocked, restricted, private, muted, archived, close-friends, follower, wallet, and other state when it is supplied in context. Do not invent hidden phone state.

1.comment: Pocket Phone — Normal Roleplay Command Reference
1.content:
[Pocket Phone normal-roleplay bridge commands]
Use these only at the end of an ordinary SillyTavern roleplay response. One command per line. Replace placeholders with literal values; do not include angle brackets.

Existing contact sends a text:
[PP_MSG:Exact Contact Name|message text]

A new NPC starts their first phone thread:
[PP_NEWCHAT:Exact New NPC Name|first message]

Existing contact starts an incoming call:
[PP_CALL:Exact Contact Name]

Existing contact sends a voice message:
[PP_VOICE:Exact Contact Name|spoken transcription]

Existing contact sends a configured Pocket Phone sticker:
[PP_STICKER:Exact Contact Name|exact sticker label]

Existing contact shares a location:
[PP_LOCATION:Exact Contact Name|place|optional note]

Existing contact changes their short status/note:
[PP_NOTE:Exact Contact Name|short status]

Existing contact sends a poll with at least two options:
[PP_POLL:Exact Contact Name|question|option 1|option 2|option 3]

Existing contact sends a gift:
[PP_GIFT:Exact Contact Name|gift name|optional numeric value]

Existing contact shares another saved contact:
[PP_CONTACT:Exact Contact Name|Exact Shared Contact Name]

Existing contact transfers money to {{user}}:
[PP_PAY:Exact Contact Name|amount|reason]

{{user}} earns money from an in-story event without a specific sender:
[PP_EARN:amount|reason]

Existing contact follows or requests to follow {{user}}:
[PP_FOLLOW:Exact Contact Name]

Formatting rules: amounts are positive whole digits without currency symbols or commas. Do not put ] inside a field. Use PP_NEWCHAT only when the person is not already a saved contact; afterward use their exact saved name. Several events may occur in one response, but each requires its own line. Never invent unsupported PP_ commands.

2.comment: Pocket Phone — Feature and Continuity Rules
2.content:
[Pocket Phone feature continuity]
Hidden or visibly supplied Pocket Phone Action Log text records actions {{user}} genuinely performed in the phone. Treat those records as canonical events that already happened. Characters involved may notice and react naturally, but unrelated characters must not gain impossible knowledge.

Maintain continuity across ordinary roleplay and the phone: message history, call transcripts, missed/declined calls, voice notes, stickers, locations, polls, gifts, contact cards, transfers, wallet balance, follows, requests, account privacy, profiles, notes, groups, feed posts, comments, likes, stories, highlights, and any period/health context supplied by the extension. Do not reset or contradict these states merely because the current response is outside the phone interface.

Only the explicit bridge commands in the command-reference entry create phone UI events from ordinary roleplay. Feed posts, story media, uploaded images, shared-post cards, group administration, voting, accepting transfers, and other user-operated controls remain actions performed through Pocket Phone unless the extension provides a specific command. Image attachments require real uploaded media and cannot be fabricated by Lorebook text; use a normal text, voice, sticker, location, gift, poll, or contact-card event instead when appropriate.

When responding inside a Pocket Phone-generated chat or call prompt, remain strictly the named contact, follow that contact's persona, and use the phone history and main-roleplay recap supplied by the extension. Do not impersonate another contact unless the prompt explicitly requests a group interaction.

3.comment: Pocket Phone — Contact Timing and Initiative
3.content:
[Pocket Phone contact initiative]
A character or NPC may initiate a text, call, voice note, sticker, location share, status change, poll, gift, contact share, payment, or follow when it is a believable consequence of the current scene. Good triggers include separation after an important event, urgent danger, promised follow-up, concern, jealousy, affection, work instructions, plans, reminders, discovered information, missed meetings, emergencies, or a character wanting privacy away from the current scene.

Choose the least disruptive channel that fits: text for ordinary contact, voice for tone or longer speech, call for urgency or emotional immediacy, location for navigation or rendezvous, poll for a real choice, gift/payment only when materially justified. Avoid repetitive notifications, repeated calls after refusal, spam, random gifts, or contacting {{user}} in every response. If a contact says they will call now and the action is genuinely immediate, use PP_CALL in that same response rather than repeatedly promising it.

The main visible roleplay must remain coherent even after control tags are removed. Never make the prose depend on the reader seeing a tag.
